about:
Edelen Renewables, based in Lexington, Kentucky, was founded in 1996. The company operates as a renewable energy developer and advisory firm, with former Georgia State Senator Jason Carter serving as strategic advisor. Carter, who also chairs The Carter Center and is a partner at Bondurant Mixson & Elmore, brings experience in clean energy advocacy and global peace initiatives. The firm's origins are not detailed in public materials.

The company focuses on solar project development and carbon-neutral strategy consulting. According to its website, Edelen Renewables builds solar partnerships and pursues gigawatt-scale solar and storage projects, citing a potential private capital investment exceeding $3 billion. No facility size, headcount, or production volumes are disclosed.

Edelen Renewables serves the renewable energy sector, with an emphasis on bringing solar power to rural and underserved communities across America. Its stated mission centers on "bringing the promise of renewable energy to the forgotten places of America." Specific customer types or named clients are not provided.

The firm differentiates itself through a stated commitment to genuine climate action and leveraging new energy for rural America. Its advisory board includes figures with political and nonprofit leadership backgrounds, though the company does not publish detailed technical differentiators or certifications.
